The training: stop and start again

Each session alternates rhythm and pause. In rhythm (blue screen), follow the beat: the speed changes every round. In the pause (red screen), take your hands off and breathe along with the waves until the countdown hits zero. At the end, the screen turns green (released: finish at your own pace) or purple (end without release).

Feel like you’re about to go past the point too early? Tap “I’m close”: the app tells you to stop right away and the pause gets longer. If you’re still close during the pause, tap again for 10 more seconds. Using it early is a sign of control, not weakness.

Easy is short and ends with a release. Medium and Hard have more rounds and faster rhythms. Impossible goes to the end without release: pure control training. In Custom you choose the rounds, times, rhythms and how it ends. On the Today screen, swipe the cards to choose a level and tap Start.

So as not to feed the rush, release has rules: after a release (or a “couldn’t hold it”, or an interrupted session), the next one only comes after the chosen interval (24 h by default). A session started less than 2 h after the previous one is control only, and with 5 or more sessions in the week the interval doubles. When it’s closed, the session isn’t canceled: it becomes control training.

Before each session the app asks to pin the screen, a feature of Android itself: while pinned, you can’t open another app, notifications and split screen are blocked, and floating videos are closed. On Android 12 or newer, floating windows from other apps also disappear. If you leave the app, the session pauses. Coming back within 10 s continues it; longer than that, or on the third exit, it ends as interrupted. To turn focus mode off, the change only applies 24 h later.

When the urge hits, open the Refuge. Breathe guides you for 2 minutes (in for 4 s, out for 6 s) with a calm soundtrack that follows your breath. The games keep your mind busy with something visual for a few minutes. The readings explain what science knows, with sources at the end.

Points reward consistency: the day’s check-in, breathing, playing, reading and the first session of the day (only with the screen pinned). The cap is %1$d points a day. Your level counts the last 28 days: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Unbeaten. Unbeaten also asks for 14 days in a row of consistency and 14 days without “couldn’t hold it” or an interrupted session. Each level unlocks a color for the app.
Short texts about mind, body and sexuality, written to inform without scaring. Each one cites the studies used. Reading to the end marks it as read and earns points once per article.

Compasso has no internet access: everything stays on this phone only, with no account. You can require a passcode on open, hide the app in recents (discreet mode) and clear the history. The codename is created by the app and doesn’t identify you.
The rules are fixed and always visible, so you know what to expect. The session is never canceled: with release closed, it becomes control training.

Urges come in waves and pass. Pick a way out and stay here until it eases.

In a field study (Skorka-Brown and colleagues, 2015), playing Tetris for 3 minutes lowered the strength of cravings for food, drink, cigarettes, coffee and also sex by 13.9 percentage points on average. The games here follow the same idea: keep your mind busy with something visual until the wave passes.
A refuge to take back control
Control training, breathing and a safe place for when the urge hits. Away from porn, at your own pace.
No account and no internet. Everything stays on this phone.
Compasso helps people who want to quit porn, without guilt. Instead of videos: control training with pauses, breathing and a safe place for when the urge hits.
Follow the beat. When the screen turns red, hands off and breathe with the waves. Feel like you’re about to go past the point? Tap “I’m close”. Over time, you notice your body sooner and last longer.
Smart control spaces out releases (24 h by default). Focus mode pins the screen during the session: no other apps, floating videos or split screen.
In the Refuge you breathe with a calm soundtrack, play for 3 minutes or read something that helps. Urges come in waves: they rise, peak and pass.
